site.title: Node site
site.intro: An ordinary website the node shows to everyone but your clients: whoever opens its address in a browser, and a scanner checking the port. REALITY borrows its own site's handshake instead of someone else's on someone else's IP; TrustTunnel answers with this site without a password (only apps on mihomo need it — VLESS is enough for many). The site serves the whole node, not one protocol.
site.required: Upload a zip of a static website. Required at its root: index.html, 404.html, robots.txt and a favicon. Static files only: no PHP or databases. Best is your own site or a popular ready-made template with your own texts. Give every node its own site, or at least its own name: one site on several nodes ties them together.
site.assigned: Site set: the node gets it within seconds.
site.cleared: The site is off the node.
site.uploaded: Site uploaded. Pick it and press Apply.
site.existing: This site is uploaded already — it is in the list under its first name.
site.severalNodes: On several nodes — ties them together
site.statusNone: The node shows no site: its address answers with the panel or nothing, and TrustTunnel without a fallback of its own answers like a proxy.
site.statusPending: The node does not serve this site yet. If that lasts over a minute, the node probably runs Mikan without sites — update it to Kinkan.
site.statusError: The node could not start the site: {error}
site.uploadHint: A zip archive up to 16 MB. An archive of one folder works too: its content is taken.
site.name: Name in the panel

ttProbe.title: Protocol probes
ttProbe.intro: Check enabled inbounds without credentials: TLS and HTTP, QUIC and HTTP/3, and responses to random bytes. Compare them with the node website.
ttProbe.vantage: Requests originate from the panel server. This checks its network path, not the client network or filtering on that path.
ttProbe.noInbound: This node has no enabled inbounds.
ttProbe.referenceHint: The HTTPS port of the cover site on this node, for example Caddy's. Leave blank to check without comparison. Certificates are verified.
ttProbe.badPort: Enter a port from 1 to 65535 or leave it blank.
ttProbe.wait: Checking inbounds sequentially. The run is limited to four minutes; closing this window cancels it.
ttProbe.limits: Cover differences need investigation. Quiet means the completed probes matched; silence, obfuscation and timing alone do not establish invisibility.
ttProbe.localNode: This node runs on the panel's server: the panel checks its own address. Some providers do not route a server to its own public IP, and then every check fails; the result says nothing about other networks.
ttProbe.verdictFAIL: The port gives itself away as a proxy: {n} signs found. Open the red rows below.
ttProbe.verdictERROR: The check is incomplete: {n} checks did not run. The rest of the result cannot be trusted as a whole.
ttProbe.verdictWARN: No explicit proxy signs. Differences from the cover site: {n}, they need review.
ttProbe.verdictPASS: No proxy signs and no differences from the cover site.
ttProbe.verdictNoReference: No explicit proxy signs. There was no comparison with a cover site, so differences are not checked.

nodeProbe.referenceHostHint: Domain without https:// or a port. Leave blank to use the inbound hostname. All connections go to the node IP.
nodeProbe.noReference: Probes run, but a Quiet verdict requires a cover site comparison. Enter the cover site HTTPS port.
nodeProbe.obfuscated: This port uses obfuscation: plain QUIC probes cannot pass it. Silence does not establish stealth.
nodeProbe.incompleteReason: Some probes failed or are unsupported. See the findings below.
nodeProbe.insufficient: The probes do not provide enough evidence to assess stealth.

scanners.title: Scanner journal
scanners.intro: Rejected requests over 30 days, aggregated by IP. No credentials or user traffic. Website visitors may be browsers; attribution is a network or verified reverse-DNS hint.
scanners.coverage: Updated Kinkan nodes record TrustTunnel, rejected REALITY handshakes, TUIC, wrong AnyTLS auth and failed Hysteria2 auth requests. Pre-QUIC obfuscation failures and other protocols are not visible yet.
scanners.spike: Increased probing: at least 100 requests today and more than three times the previous 7-day daily average.
scanners.showClients: Show errors from known client addresses
scanners.empty: No records yet. Collection requires an updated node; historical scans cannot be recovered.
scanners.geoSource: Country and network, where the node found none, from the panel's database:

quietNode.title: Quiet node

verdict.quiet: The node looks like an ordinary website: no inbound gave it away.
verdict.noticeable: The node stands out: some inbounds answer unlike an ordinary website. Which, and what to do, below.
verdict.exposed: The node gives itself away. One such port is enough for a scanner to learn the address, and blocking the address cuts every protocol on it at once.
verdict.inconclusive: Not every inbound could be judged. A node is quiet only when each inbound was checked.

advice.tuic_auth: TUIC answers a wrong password with its own close code: that is the protocol, no setting hides it. Keep TUIC on a separate node with another address, or turn it off here.
advice.quic_obfs: Hysteria2 without obfs answers strangers like a proxy. Turn on obfs (Salamander) in the inbound's settings: without the password the port stays silent. Clients get the new subscription by themselves.
advice.quic_auth: This QUIC inbound answers strangers like a proxy even with obfs. Turn it off here or move it to a separate node.
advice.tt_site: TrustTunnel without a site answers strangers "407 — proxy authentication required". Give the node a site: TrustTunnel shows it by itself.
advice.tt_differs: TrustTunnel shows a site, but its answers differ from the reference. What differs is in the check's details below.
advice.reality_site: REALITY shows the panel's empty 404 instead of a site. Give the node a site: REALITY switches to it by itself.
advice.reality_differs: The REALITY target does not answer like an ordinary website. Check that a live site with this certificate stands behind the SNI; details below.
advice.exposed: The inbound answers strangers like a proxy. Turn it off here or move it to a separate node.
advice.noticeable: The inbound's answers differ from an ordinary website. Details below.
advice.no_reference: There was nothing to compare with. Check again with a reference: usually port 443, where REALITY shows the node's site.
advice.obfuscated: The port is silent without the password, as it should be with obfs. Nothing more can be checked from outside.
advice.incomplete: The check did not finish or the protocol is not supported yet. That does not mean quiet.
advice.reality_far: The REALITY target "{target}" lives in another network (AS{target_as} {target_org}) than the node (AS{node_as} {node_org}). A scanner sees that site's certificate on a hosting address, a known sign of REALITY. Pick a target near the server (Protocols → the inbound → Find near the server) or give the node its own site.

quietNode.disableText: Clients lose this inbound: it is gone at their next subscription update. Turn it back on under Protocols.
quietNode.why: A node is no quieter than its loudest inbound: all protocols share its address.
